Drug Antagonism.question: 1) Physiological antagonism means:
Drug Antagonism.option1: Two drugs react chemically and neutralize each other
Drug Antagonism.option2: Two drugs compete for the same receptor reversibly
Drug Antagonism.option3: One drug blocks absorption of another drug only
Drug Antagonism.option4: Two agonists act on different receptors and produce opposite physiological effects
Drug Antagonism.exp: Physiological antagonism occurs through different receptors. The final physiological effects are opposite. Acetylcholine and adrenaline are examples.

Drug Antagonism.question: 2) Which pair is an example of physiological antagonism?
Drug Antagonism.exp: Histamine and adrenaline act on different receptors. Their physiological effects may oppose each other. This is physiological antagonism.

Drug Antagonism.question: 3) Chemical antagonism means:
Drug Antagonism.exp: Chemical antagonism occurs when two agents react chemically. One neutralizes the other. Antacid and gastric HCl are examples.

Drug Antagonism.question: 4) Antacid and gastric HCl represent:
Drug Antagonism.exp: Antacid chemically neutralizes gastric acid. This does not require receptor blockade. So it is chemical antagonism.

Drug Antagonism.question: 5) Iron poisoning treated with desferrioxamine is an example of:
Drug Antagonism.exp: Desferrioxamine binds iron chemically. This reduces free toxic iron. It is a chelation-type chemical antagonism.

Drug Antagonism.question: 6) Pharmacological antagonism means:
Drug Antagonism.option2: Two chemicals neutralize each other in solution
Drug Antagonism.option3: Agonist and antagonist act at the same receptor
Drug Antagonism.option4: Two drugs act on different receptors
Drug Antagonism.exp: Pharmacological antagonism occurs at the same receptor. An antagonist blocks agonist effect. Competitive antagonism may be overcome by increasing agonist.

Drug Antagonism.question: 7) Atropine and acetylcholine at muscarinic receptor represent:
Drug Antagonism.exp: Atropine blocks muscarinic receptors. Acetylcholine acts on the same receptor. This is receptor-level pharmacological antagonism.

Drug Antagonism.question: 8) Morphine and naloxone at opioid receptor represent:
Drug Antagonism.exp: Naloxone antagonizes morphine at opioid receptors. It acts at the same receptor system. It is a classic competitive pharmacological antagonist.

Drug Antagonism.question: 9) Catecholamines and propranolol at beta receptor represent:
Drug Antagonism.exp: Propranolol blocks beta receptors. Catecholamines stimulate beta receptors. Both act at the same receptor system.

Drug Antagonism.question: 10) Competitive pharmacological antagonism may be overcome by increasing:
Drug Antagonism.exp: In competitive antagonism, agonist and antagonist compete at receptor. Increasing agonist concentration can overcome reversible competitive blockade. Naloxone and morphine are a classic example.

Drug Antagonism.question: 11) Drugs that cross the blood-brain barrier are usually:
Drug Antagonism.exp: Lipid-soluble drugs cross BBB more easily. Highly ionized and large molecules enter CNS poorly. This explains why CNS drugs are often lipophilic.

Drug Antagonism.question: 12) Thiopental crosses the blood-brain barrier because it is:
Drug Antagonism.exp: Thiopental is lipid-soluble. It rapidly enters the brain. This explains its rapid CNS action.

Drug Antagonism.question: 13) Which drug crosses the blood-brain barrier?
Drug Antagonism.exp: Atropine is a tertiary amine. It can cross the BBB. Quaternary ammonium drugs like glycopyrrolate enter CNS poorly.

Drug Antagonism.question: 14) Which drug has poor CNS entry?
Drug Antagonism.exp: Glycopyrrolate is a quaternary ammonium compound. It poorly crosses the BBB. So it has fewer central anticholinergic effects.

Drug Antagonism.question: 15) Ipratropium has poor CNS entry because it is:
Drug Antagonism.exp: Ipratropium is quaternary ammonium. It is poorly lipid-soluble and poorly crosses BBB. This limits central nervous system effects.

Drug Antagonism.question: 16) Which drug crosses BBB?
Drug Antagonism.exp: Physostigmine crosses the BBB. Neostigmine is quaternary and enters CNS poorly. This distinction is important in cholinergic pharmacology.

Drug Antagonism.question: 17) Which substance crosses BBB?
Drug Antagonism.exp: Ethanol readily crosses the BBB. It produces central nervous system effects. Its lipid solubility helps brain penetration.

Drug Antagonism.question: 18) Which antimicrobial crosses BBB according to the listed group?
Drug Antagonism.exp: Chloramphenicol is listed among drugs crossing BBB. Some sulfonamides and third-generation cephalosporins also cross. CNS penetration is important for meningitis treatment.

Drug Antagonism.question: 19) Third-generation cephalosporins are listed as drugs that:
Drug Antagonism.exp: Third-generation cephalosporins can cross BBB. This makes them useful in CNS infections. Earlier-generation cephalosporins usually have poorer CNS entry.

Drug Antagonism.question: 20) Most first-generation cephalosporins:
Drug Antagonism.exp: Most first-generation cephalosporins do not cross BBB well. Third-generation cephalosporins cross better. Generation affects CNS penetration.

Drug Antagonism.question: 21) Which drug crosses BBB?
Drug Antagonism.exp: Morphine crosses the BBB and produces CNS effects. It causes analgesia, sedation and respiratory depression. Poor CNS entry drugs show fewer central effects.

Drug Antagonism.question: 22) Dopamine does not cross BBB well; therefore in Parkinson disease we use:
Drug Antagonism.exp: Dopamine has poor CNS entry. Levodopa crosses into the brain and converts to dopamine. This is a classic BBB-based therapeutic strategy.

Drug Antagonism.question: 23) Carbidopa has poor CNS entry and is used mainly to inhibit peripheral:
Drug Antagonism.exp: Carbidopa does not cross BBB well. It inhibits peripheral conversion of levodopa to dopamine. This increases levodopa availability to brain and reduces peripheral adverse effects.

Drug Antagonism.question: 24) Benzodiazepines are listed among drugs that:
Drug Antagonism.exp: Benzodiazepines cross the BBB. They act on CNS benzodiazepine receptors. This produces anxiolytic, sedative and anticonvulsant effects.

Drug Antagonism.question: 25) Which drug has poor CNS entry?
Drug Antagonism.exp: Neostigmine is poorly lipid-soluble and quaternary. It does not cross BBB well. Physostigmine crosses BBB better.

Drug Antagonism.question: 26) Which drug crosses the placental barrier?
Drug Antagonism.exp: Warfarin crosses placenta. It may cause fetal warfarin syndrome. Heparin does not cross placenta significantly.

Drug Antagonism.question: 27) Which anticoagulant is safer in pregnancy because it does not cross placenta?
Drug Antagonism.exp: Heparin is large and does not cross placenta. Therefore it is preferred when anticoagulation is needed in pregnancy. Warfarin crosses placenta and can harm the fetus.

Drug Antagonism.question: 28) Which CNS drug crosses the placental barrier?
Drug Antagonism.exp: Phenytoin crosses the placenta. It can cause fetal hydantoin syndrome. Antiepileptic selection in pregnancy needs special caution.

Drug Antagonism.question: 29) Valproate crosses placenta and is associated with:
Drug Antagonism.exp: Valproate crosses placenta. It is associated with neural tube defects such as spina bifida. It is an important teratogenic antiepileptic.

Drug Antagonism.question: 30) Isotretinoin crosses placenta and is known for:
Drug Antagonism.exp: Isotretinoin is highly teratogenic. It crosses the placenta and may cause severe fetal malformations. Pregnancy prevention is essential during treatment.

Drug Antagonism.question: 31) Radioiodine crosses placenta and may affect fetal:
Drug Antagonism.exp: Radioiodine crosses placenta. It can affect fetal thyroid tissue. Therefore it is contraindicated in pregnancy.

Drug Antagonism.question: 32) Live vaccines are listed among substances that:
Drug Antagonism.option1: Cross placental barrier and need caution
Drug Antagonism.option4: Do not affect fetus at all
Drug Antagonism.exp: Live vaccines are listed among substances crossing placenta. They are generally avoided during pregnancy. The concern is potential fetal infection or harm.

Drug Antagonism.question: 33) Vincristine crosses placenta and belongs to:
Drug Antagonism.exp: Vincristine is an anticancer drug. It crosses placenta. Anticancer drugs generally need careful risk-benefit assessment in pregnancy.

Drug Antagonism.question: 34) Metformin is listed under placental-crossing drugs in the category of:
Drug Antagonism.exp: Metformin is listed among antidiabetic drugs crossing placenta. Placental transfer does not automatically mean absolute contraindication. Pregnancy drug choice depends on safety record and clinical need.

Drug Antagonism.question: 35) The most accurate barrier-related statement is:
Drug Antagonism.option1: Quaternary ammonium drugs cross BBB freely
Drug Antagonism.option2: Lipid-soluble drugs cross BBB more easily
Drug Antagonism.exp: Lipid-soluble drugs penetrate BBB better. Quaternary ammonium compounds have poor CNS entry. Warfarin crosses placenta, while heparin does not.
